description: How the agent's optimization concepts COMPOSE. Two layers of pipeline knowledge: (1) `enables` relations between concepts — concept A creates conditions concept B can fire on; (2) named `Pipeline` orderings — canonical sequences a compiler runs to fixed point. The agent's reasoning about pass ordering becomes a graph traversal: which concept follows which, what does my pipeline cover, where would a new optimization fit. The substrate's own behavior already exhibits these cascades (reassoc→constfold→DCE collapses (x+1)+2 to x+3 in a single run_rules call after the engine fix), but the cascades are observation; this seed promotes them to declarative knowledge.

enables.rationale: Right-associating (a op b) op c → a op (b op c) when a is a variable and b, c are constants pulls the two constants into the inner instruction's operand pair — exactly the shape constfold matches. Tested live: (x + 1) + 2 collapses to x + 3.

Constfold may produce a constant whose value is the operator's identity (0 for add/or/xor, 1 for mul, -1 for and). The new constant then satisfies an identity rule's value-eq side-condition, exposing further elimination.

icmp constfold (a constant_folding member) produces an i1 constant. If that constant flows into a select instruction's condition operand, the select becomes statically determined and select_constant_condition fires — the canonical `compare-then-choose` cascade collapses entirely.

The same i1 constant produced by icmp constfold can flow into a `br_cond` instruction's condition operand. The conditional branch then has a statically-known target and folds to an unconditional branch — the control-flow analogue of the icmp+select cascade. Subsequent dead-block elimination cleans up the unreachable branch.

Folding a br_cond to an unconditional br removes the branch's reference to the non-taken target. The non-taken basic block may now have no incoming references — a candidate for dead-block elimination.
After the select is eliminated and its uses rewired, the un-chosen branch's producer may have lost its only consumer and become dead — DCE cleans it up.
Similar to select_constant_condition: rewiring around the select may make its operands' producers dead.
Constfold replaces every use of an old instruction's result with the constant, then deletes the instruction. Operands that were only feeding that instruction may now have zero uses, becoming dead.
Identity rules rewire uses to the non-trivial operand and delete the instruction; the constant operand may then have zero uses and itself become dead.
CSE rewires uses of the duplicate to the canonical and deletes the duplicate. Operands that fed only the duplicate may have lost all their uses and become dead.
Strength reduction rewires the multiplier constant out and replaces it with the shift-amount constant. The old constant has lost its only use and becomes dead.
sub(X, X) → 0 and xor(X, X) → 0 materialise zero constants whose uses then become candidates for constfold or identity rules in the consumer instructions.
Eliminating one duplicate may expose another — e.g. if (x + y) was duplicated and is itself a subexpression of another duplicated expression, the cleanup cascades.

Deleting an instruction may make its operands dead too — classic DCE-to-fixed-point cascade. The engine fix in this session makes this work in a single run_rules call by clearing eval_cache + bumping edge_delete_version after each delete-bearing rule fires.

pipelines.name: minimal_peephole
pipelines.description: The smallest useful pass set: fold constants, then clean dead code. Sufficient for trivial input programs but leaves algebraic structure unsimplified.

pipelines.name: local_peephole
pipelines.description: Full local-rewriting pipeline. Normalize first (reassociation pulls constants adjacent), then reduce (constfold + select simplification + control-flow constant folding), then eliminate (algebraic identities, CSE), strength-reduce, finally clean dead code. Run to fixed point — passes feed each other, e.g. icmp constfold → select_constant_condition or control_flow_constant_folding → DCE collapses compare-then-branch (and compare-then-choose) chains entirely.

pipelines.name: dce_only
pipelines.description: Just clean up dead code. Useful as a final cleanup pass after global transformations that may have orphaned local computations.
